meta.title: Operation of Magnetic Stirrer in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To provide controlled, continuous magnetic stirring for dissolving crude drug extracts, preparing reagent solutions, and maintaining homogeneity of liquid mixtures during phytochemical analyses.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for all operations requiring continuous liquid mixing without mechanical contact, including preparation of extraction solvents, colour development assays, and standard solutions.
procedure: Place the magnetic stirrer on a stable, level bench surface.
Select an appropriate PTFE-coated magnetic stir bar (flea) of size proportional to the vessel: small flea for test tubes and small beakers; larger flea for 250–1000 mL flasks.
Drop the stir bar gently into the vessel containing the liquid to be stirred.
Place the vessel centrally on the magnetic stirrer plate.
Connect the stirrer to the power supply and switch on.
Slowly increase the speed using the speed control knob from zero upward — rapid acceleration can cause the stir bar to spin eccentrically and 'jump'.
Set the optimal stirring speed: slow (50–100 RPM) for gentle mixing of fragile precipitates; medium (200–400 RPM) for dissolving solids; high (500–700 RPM) for vigorous mixing.
Observe the vortex formation — a slight vortex is acceptable; a deep vortex introduces air bubbles which interfere with optical measurements.
Allow stirring for the required duration.
After use, reduce speed to zero before switching off — abrupt stopping can cause the stir bar to fly off.
Use a stir bar retriever (magnetic wand) to remove the stir bar from the vessel.
Rinse the stir bar with distilled water and appropriate solvent, then store.
Wipe the stirrer plate clean of spills — never immerse the stirrer unit in liquid.
precautions: Do not use a magnetic stirrer with strong oxidizing acids (aqua regia, fuming acids) — the PTFE stir bar is resistant but the plate and housing may corrode.
Do not exceed the rated stirring capacity of the unit — over-speed causes erratic bar movement ('bar dancing').
If the stir bar 'dances' erratically, reduce speed immediately, remove, and restart from zero.
Do not use magnetic stirrers with ferrous metallic vessels or near strong permanent magnets.
For heating combined with stirring (hot plate-stirrer): monitor temperature separately with a calibrated thermometer — the plate temperature reading alone is not the actual solution temperature.
Ensure the vessel is secure — a wobbling, clamp-free vessel can be dislodged by the stirring action.
Clean the stirrer plate after each use — spilled chemicals corrode the plate surface.
